questions.question: The efforts of Siddhendra Yogi have brought glory to the dance form called ______.
questions.solution:
Siddhendra Yogi was a legendary scholar and saint who is considered the Adi Guru (first teacher) of Kuchipudi. He is credited with systemizing the dance form and composing the famous dance-drama Bhama Kalapam.

Note: Kuchipudi is a classical dance from Andhra Pradesh that combines fast footwork and dramatic storytelling.

questions.question: Which of the following is a UNESCO recognised dance form?
questions.solution:
Kalbelia is a folk dance from Rajasthan that was included in UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010. It is performed by the tribe of the same name, often called the Snake Charmer tribe, where dancers mimic the movements of a cobra.

Related Info: The dance is accompanied by the Pungi, a woodwind instrument traditionally used to charm snakes.

questions.question: Me-Dum-Me-Phi is an ancestor-worship festival celebrated in the state of ______.
questions.solution:
Me-Dum-Me-Phi is the most important ancestor-worship festival celebrated by the Ahom people of Assam on 31st January every year. 'Me' means offerings, 'Dam' means ancestors, and 'Phi' means gods.

Note: It is observed to show respect to the departed and seek their blessings for communal harmony.

questions.question: From which of the following English words is the name ‘Bhangra’ derived in the context of Bhangra Dance?
questions.solution:
In the context of the energetic Punjabi dance, the name Bhangra is derived from the word Hemp (specifically Bhang). Historically, the dance was performed by farmers during the harvest season of hemp/cannabis.

Additional Info: It is a vigorous dance usually performed to the beats of the Dhol to celebrate the Baisakhi festival.

questions.question: ______ is a form of ballad singing prevalent in Odisha.
questions.solution:
Daskathia is a popular form of ballad singing or folk theater prevalent in Odisha. It is performed by a duo where the lead singer (Gahaka) narrates mythological stories accompanied by a small percussion instrument called the Kathi (wooden clappers).

Note: It is traditionally dedicated to Lord Shiva.

questions.question: ‘Ummatt-aat’ is a folk dance form performed in ______.
questions.solution:
Ummatt-aat is a traditional folk dance performed in the Coorg (Kodagu) region of Karnataka. Dressed in traditional Kodava attire, women dance in a circle to the beats of brass symbols while carrying pots on their heads to honor the River Cauvery.

Location Note: Coorg is often referred to as the 'Scotland of India'.

questions.question: ‘Ponung’ and ‘Tapu’ are popular dance forms from the state of ______ .
questions.solution:
Ponung and Tapu are significant folk dances of Arunachal Pradesh. Ponung is a dance performed by women of the Adi tribe to pray for a good harvest, while Tapu is a vigorous War Dance performed by men to drive away evil spirits.

Note: These dances are central to the socio-religious life of the tribal communities in the Northeast.

questions.question: A ‘Nattuvanar’ conducts a ______ dance recital.
questions.solution:
A Nattuvanar is the conductor or the master of ceremonies in a Bharatanatyam recital. They are responsible for keeping the rhythm using Cymbals (Talam) and chanting the rhythmic syllables (Sollukattu).

Key Fact: Traditionally, the Nattuvanar was also the teacher or Guru who trained the dancer.

questions.question: Which of the following is a dance form that originated in Assam?
questions.solution:
Sattriya is a classical dance form that originated in the Sattras (monasteries) of Assam. It was introduced by the great saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th century as a medium for propagating Vaishnavism.

Note: It was recognized as a Classical Dance of India by Sangeet Natak Akademi in the year 2000.

questions.question: Lalita is a form of folk music from ______.
questions.solution:
Lalita is a form of folk music or religious performance from Maharashtra. It is similar to Tamasha but is more focused on religious storytelling and the glorification of deities through songs and enactments.

Related Info: Maharashtra is also famous for other folk forms like Lavani and Bharud.

questions.question: Which of the following is a folk song genre popular in parts of West Bengal, Assam and Bangladesh?
questions.solution:
Bhawaiya is a popular folk song genre found in Northern West Bengal, Assam (Goalpara region), and Bangladesh. It is traditionally sung by Mahouts (elephant trainers) and cart drivers, characterized by a unique 'break' in the voice that conveys deep emotion.

Note: It typically deals with themes of longing and the hardships of daily life.

questions.question: ______ is a popular folk dance of Minicoy Island.
questions.solution:
Lava is the most popular folk dance of the Minicoy Island in the Union Territory of Lakshadweep. It is performed by men in colorful costumes to the accompaniment of drums and rhythmic chanting.

Context: Minicoy is the southernmost atoll of Lakshadweep and has a culture distinct from the other islands.

questions.question: Kelucharan Mohapatra was an exponent of which of the following categories of dance?
questions.solution:
Kelucharan Mohapatra was a legendary Indian classical dancer, guru, and proponent of Odissi. He is credited with the 20th-century revival of this ancient dance form from Odisha.

Note: He was the first person from Odisha to receive the Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: ______ is a mask dance popular in South Malabar.
questions.solution:
Kummattikali is a famous mask dance prevalent in the South Malabar region (specifically Thrissur and Palakkad) of Kerala. Dancers wear brightly painted wooden masks and cover their bodies with grass or leaves to represent characters from the Ramayana or folk deities.

Festival: It is primarily performed during the Onam festival.

questions.question: In which of the following dances do dancers balance pots containing lit lamps on their heads?
questions.solution:
The Chari dance is a traditional folk dance of the Guijar community in Rajasthan (Kishangarh). In this dance, women demonstrate immense skill by balancing brass pots (Chari) on their heads, which contain burning cotton seeds soaked in oil.

Visual Note: The lit lamps create a stunning visual effect during night performances.

questions.question: ‘Povadas’ is a popular folk dance from the state of ______.
questions.solution:
Povadas (or Pawada) is a popular folk dance and ballad form from Maharashtra. It typically narrates the life and brave deeds of historical figures, most notably Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

Style: The singers are known as Shahirs, and the performance is characterized by its high energy and patriotic themes.

questions.question: A Ghatam is a ______.
questions.option_1: large, narrow-mouthed earthenware pot used as a percussion instrument
questions.option_2: small handheld drum that resembles a tambourine
questions.option_3: wind instrument made of wood and metal
questions.option_4: percussion instrument made of leather and jackwood
questions.solution:
A Ghatam is a large earthenware pot with a narrow mouth, used as a percussion instrument in Carnatic music. Unlike a regular pot, it is made of special clay and sometimes contains metal filings to produce a sharp, metallic ring.

Classification: It belongs to the Membranophone-adjacent family but is technically an Idiophone.

questions.question: Which of the following musical instruments did Dwaram Venkataswamy Naidu play?
questions.solution:
Dwaram Venkataswamy Naidu was a renowned 20th-century carnatic musician who played the Violin. He was instrumental in establishing the violin as a solo instrument in the Indian classical tradition.

Honors: He served as the Professor of Violin at the Maharajah's Government College of Music and Dance in Vizianagaram.

questions.question: ______ is a vocal form of music from the state of Punjab.
questions.solution:
Tappa is a form of Indian semi-classical vocal music that originated from the folk songs of camel riders in Punjab. It is characterized by its fast-paced, complex, and rolling tanas (rhythmic phrases).

Legacy: It was further refined and popularized in the court of the Nawab of Awadh.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a percussion instrument?
questions.solution:
A Sarod is a stringed instrument (chordophone), not a percussion instrument. It is used primarily in Hindustani classical music and is known for its deep, introspective sound and lack of frets.

Note: Ghatam, Tabla, and Mridangam are all percussion instruments used to provide rhythm.

questions.question: Which of the following musical instruments is also known as a ‘Mangal Vadya’?
questions.solution:
The Shehnai is considered a Mangal Vadya (auspicious instrument) in India. Because of its soulful and melodious sound, it is traditionally played during marriages and at temples to signify a sacred beginning.

Legend: Ustad Bismillah Khan is the most famous exponent who brought the Shehnai to the global stage.

questions.question: Who among the following Indian musicians was a part of a band named ‘Planet Drum’ along with Mickey Hart, Sikiru Adepoju, and Giovanni Hidalgo, whose first album received the 1992 Grammy Award for Best World Music Album, which was the first Grammy in this category?
questions.solution:
Zakir Hussain, the legendary Tabla maestro, was a founding member of the global percussion ensemble Planet Drum. Their self-titled debut album won the first-ever Grammy Award for Best World Music Album in 1992.

Note: This achievement highlighted the fusion of Indian percussion with global rhythms.

questions.question: Makaravilakku festival is celebrated at the sacred grove of Lord Ayyappa in:
questions.solution:
The Makaravilakku festival is a magnificent annual event held on Makar Sankranti at the Sabarimala Temple in Kerala. It marks the appearance of a celestial light (Makaravilakku) three times on the Ponnambalamedu hill.

Deity: The temple is dedicated to Lord Ayyappa, a deity particularly revered in South India.

questions.question: Splashing the mud and racing across the fields, the roaring buffalos raced by a man are typical sights for which of the following festivals of Karnataka?
questions.solution:
Kambala is a traditional buffalo race held annually in the coastal districts of Karnataka (Dakshina Kannada and Udupi). A pair of buffalos, driven by a whip-lashing farmer, race through slushy paddy fields.

Note: It is a sport originally dedicated to Lord Kadri Manjunatha to ensure a good harvest.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Ramsar convention to promote conservation and wise use of all wetlands through regional actions and international cooperation come to force in India?
questions.solution:
The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands. While it was signed in 1971, it officially came into force in India on February 1, 1982.

Status: Today, India has a large number of designated Ramsar Sites, such as Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park.

questions.question: The ______ festival of Sikkim is also known as Bhoomi Puja or Chandi Puja.
questions.solution:
Sakewa is one of the most important festivals of the Rai community in Sikkim. It is known as Bhoomi Puja or Chandi Puja, where people pray to Mother Earth for protection and a bountiful harvest.

Ceremony: The ritual involves a dance called Silli which mimics the movements of animals and birds.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is held on a new moon day?
questions.solution:
Kali Puja is celebrated on the New Moon day (Amavasya) of the Hindu month of Kartik, coinciding with the Diwali festival in many parts of India. It is dedicated to the goddess Kali, symbolizing the victory of light over darkness.

Contrast: Holi and Mahavir Jayanti are usually celebrated on full moon days (Purnima).

questions.question: ‘Sangken’ is a festival of the ______.
questions.solution:
Sangken is the traditional New Year festival of the Buddhist communities, particularly the Theravada Buddhists in Arunachal Pradesh and parts of Assam. It is a Water Festival similar to Songkran in Thailand.

Ritual: People sprinkle clean water on Buddha idols and each other as a symbol of purity and peace.

questions.question: In which Indian state is the ‘Fatorpa Zatra’ celebrated?
questions.solution:
The Fatorpa Zatra is a famous temple festival celebrated in the village of Fatorpa in Goa. It is dedicated to Goddess Shantadurga Fatorpeakarin and features grand processions of chariots (Rathas).

Note: It is a significant cultural event that draws devotees from various communities in Goa.

questions.question: ______ is an annual three-day festival held at Bara Shaheed Dargah in Nellore.
questions.solution:
Rottela Panduga (Festival of Breads) is an annual three-day Urs held at the Bara Shaheed Dargah in Nellore, Andhra Pradesh. Devotees exchange rotis (flatbreads) in the waters of the Swarnala Cheruvu tank as a thanksgiving for fulfilled wishes.

Significance: It symbolizes communal harmony and attracts people of all faiths.

questions.question: The festival of Durga Puja is observed to celebrate the triumph of Goddess Durga over ______.
questions.solution:
The festival of Durga Puja commemorates the victory of Goddess Durga over the buffalo demon Mahishasura. This triumph represents the victory of Dharma (good) over Adharma (evil).

Cultural Fact: The festival is most grandly celebrated in West Bengal and was recently recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated in Uttarakhand?
questions.solution:
Phool Dei is an auspicious harvest festival celebrated in the state of Uttarakhand. During the festival, young girls go from house to house putting flowers and rice on doorsteps to welcome the spring season.

Note: The term 'Dei' refers to a ceremonial pudding made from jaggery and flour that is shared among neighbors.
